# KartUI components

Author interfaces as `.kui` single-file components. The CLI discovers screens
and children under `ui/` or `assets/ui/`, and reusable layouts under `ui/layouts/`.
Use `karty.toml` for explicit overrides or files outside those conventions.
`ui/views/` and `ui/components/` are useful organizational conventions.
`game.ui` is one active root; calling a child component mounts it inside that root.

## Single-file components

Save this as `inventory.kui`; the filename supplies the component name `Inventory`.
The template is required. Script and style blocks are optional.

```kui
<template>
  <panel modal="true" onBack={props.Close} class="screen">
    <label>Inventory</label>
    <button enabled={props.Count() > 0} onClick={props.Close}>Close</button>
  </panel>
</template>

<script setup lang="go">
type InventoryProps struct {
    Count func() int
    Close func()
}

func setup(props InventoryProps) {}
</script>

<style>
.screen
  width: 80%
  height: 60%
  padding: 16px
  gap: 8px
  align: stretch
</style>
```

SDK 0.0.9 candidate supports the new widgets and explicit dimensions. Dimensions
use presentation schema 11; widgets use schema 10. The compiler accepts only
`.kui` single-file components. Legacy declarations and `.ui` authoring files
must be migrated.

`func setup(props Type)` runs once per mounted instance. Its locals and closures
are instance-local and available in template expressions. Call `invalidate()`
after changing UI-local state outside an automatically invalidating widget change
handler. Retained children receive fresh props when their parent invalidates.
The script accepts imports, types, and one final `setup` function without results.
Move shared helpers into ordinary Go source files. `invalidate` and names starting
with `_karty` are reserved for the generated adapter.

Block attributes may be reordered, whitespace may vary, and quoted attributes
accept single or double quotes. `<script lang='go' setup>` is equivalent to the
opening above. HTML comments may appear before, between, or after blocks.
Duplicate blocks/attributes, unsupported attributes and malformed structure remain
errors. A file contains at most one script, template and style block.

Use [indented styles](indented-styles.md) for the default compact style syntax,
[the property reference](styles.md) for supported values, and
[the settings example](../widgets.md) for all value widgets.

## Markup

| Element         | Attributes                                                 | Notes                                      |
| --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `panel`         | `class`; root: `modal="true                                | false"`, modal `onBack={ func() }`         | Root must be a panel; nested panels create layout parents. |
| `label`         | `class`                                                    | Static text is its body.                   |
| `image`         | `class`                                                    | Style `image` chooses a typed theme image. |
| `button`        | `class`, `enabled={ bool }`, `onClick={ func() }`          | Leaf control.                              |
| `list`          | `class`, `rows={ []UIRow }`, `onClick={ func(uint32) }`    | Host-owned rows.                           |
| `ComponentName` | `props={ TypedValue }`; in a loop `key={ stringOrUint32 }` | Must be an exported project component.     |
| `fragment`      | `slot="name"`                                              | Only while invoking a layout.              |
| `slot`          | optional `name="name"`                                     | Only inside a layout template.             |

Dynamic attributes use Go expressions in `{ ... }`. `class` is one CSS
identifier, not a list. Panels cannot be controls; labels do not click; controls are leaves except `tabs`/`tab` containers. Unknown attributes fail compilation.
Non-whitespace text must be inside an open `label`, `button` or literal `checkbox` caption; text after a
closed control or outside the root panel fails compilation.

## Composition, loops, and conditions

Children take one typed props argument:

```html
<ItemRow props={ ItemRowProps{ ID: id, Use: props.Use } } />
```

Only child components may occur in a range, which requires a stable `string`
(max 128 UTF-8 bytes) or `uint32` key. Keys preserve setup state on reordering;
array positions are not identity.

```go
for _, item := range props.Items() {
    <ItemRow key={ item.ID } props={ ItemRowProps{Item: item} } />
}
```

`if condition { ... } else { ... }` conditionally projects ordinary markup.
Use a child component instead of nested range loops. Cycles, duplicate keys,
duplicate slot fills, recursive layouts, and unsupported markup fail. Limits per
root: 256 instances, depth 16, 1,024 elements, 4,096 list rows.
Nested conditions and nested ranges require child components.

Each compiled component template supports at most 64 elements, with element
depth at most 15 below its implicit root panel. Reused layouts count toward
these same limits after expansion; oversized expansion stops during compilation.
The limits above for a mounted root include its retained child instances.

Static level templates cannot contain client bindings, including `if` visibility
conditions. Even a literal `if false` requires a client component; the compiler
does not evaluate authored Go expressions or discard branches when building
static presentation assets.

## Layouts and navigation

A layout SFC has one root panel, slots and local styles, with no script or
runtime asset name. Direct children fill `<slot/>`; named
`<fragment slot="...">` fills named slots. `onBack={ fn }` is the only layout
invocation attribute and assigns its semantic Back callback. Escape and gamepad
East/Back activate it. Modal roots consume game input. In SDK 0.0.8
with UI schema 9, a `modal="false"` root can contain buttons and lists while
keyboard and pointer events continue to the game. This supports movement keys
with visible touch controls. Handle scene pointer actions accordingly, because
a button click also produces the ordinary game pointer release. Nonmodal roots
cannot declare `onBack`; handle Escape in the game when needed. Schemas 1–8
retain their noninteractive HUD restriction. Touch/focus/scroll are host
behavior; callbacks are the client-visible action boundary.

Interactive controls may also live in child components. Project compilation
selects schema 9 for a nonmodal component whose descendants contain buttons or
lists, including controls reached through nested, conditional, or keyed child
composition. The root schema governs interaction for its whole mounted tree;
modal components and noninteractive HUDs keep their existing schema requirements.

## SDK 0.0.9 widgets

See [the widget reference](../widgets.md) for checkbox, combo, input, slider, tabs and tooltip syntax. These additions require SDK 0.0.9 (API 0.0.7, schema 10).

## Scoped layout styles

Layout files use `<template>` and optional `<style>` blocks, with slots in their
panel tree and no script. The filename supplies the layout name. Styles affect
only markup authored by that layout. Slot fills keep their caller's styles;
fallback slot content keeps the layout's styles. Nested layouts have independent
scopes, even when both use a class named `.content`.

To override a layout class from the consuming component, qualify its class with
the layout name. `Frame.content` targets `.content` authored by the `Frame` layout.
This applies to every instance of that layout in the component. It also accepts
states, such as `Frame.primary:hover`, and responsive overrides. Unqualified
`.content` affects only markup authored by the consuming component. Element rules
apply before class rules; explicit layout overrides apply after the layout's own
rules for that selector. Qualified selectors are for layout classes, not general
CSS descendant matching or styling inside runtime child components.

## Diagnostics

Ignored styles produce warnings with `file:line:column` locations in the original
component or layout file. Columns are one-based byte positions. Structural block
errors, indentation errors, Go script/expression syntax errors and invalid markup attributes
also identify authored locations. `Component.Diagnostics()` returns structured
style warnings; `StyleWarnings()` returns formatted strings. `SourceError` exposes
compiler error locations and preserves its cause for `errors.Is`/`errors.As`.
Go type errors from generated client compilation may still refer to generated Go;
this compiler does not replace Go type checking or provide editor diagnostics.
